items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Frank Galbraight had come back and Wallace Wilson and Arthur Trappier, one the ex-Fats Waller drummer had replaced Wallace Bishop.

ctx.x: In Ohio, Frank Galbraith met some friends he had known for a long time, and as Sy didn't have any more jobs for a while, Frank stayed in this town. He was the first person that I ever knew that called everybody "Baby". If something was wrong, for example, a certain phrase in an arrangement, and Frank felt that he knew how it should go, he would say to the one that did not grasp the idea: "No Baby, it doesn't go like that." At one time, only a girl that a fellow may have liked, was called "Baby", but now, anyone -…

June the 27th, we played the Apollo again. Pearl Bailey was the featured attraction and Cosy Cole had a revue of dancers and Tom-Tom players. I had been in an Edgar Hayes band that played some theatre dates in Atlantic City, New Jersey, Pennsylvania with Pearl before she became a big star in the early 40's. Bill "Bojangle" Robinson was the star of the show. Now I was hearing Pearl as a big star, and Sy's band was breaking a record by bearing the only band to play a return engagement in the Apollo within six…

Sy was quite a difficult leader to work with. He didn't have the same hospitable feeling that Benny Carter had. He's one that considers musicians to be like children - he's the father, and your're the kids. He actually used to address us as "You Kids" sometimes. He didn't mean any harm by it, it was just his way of behaving. He was a good ground man on trumpet - not a lead player, but a good second or third trumpet player that didn't take too many solos.
